subject: using colext to look at how habitat change influences occupancy dynamics

messages.author: 0f206837070c34f7
messages.subject: using colext to look at how habitat change influences occupancy dynamics
parts:
Hi All -- 

I have a data set with bird (presence/absence) and habitat information from 2 time periods, about 25 years apart. I would like to look at how colonization/extinction/persistence is related to change in habitat class between the 2 time periods.

The Mackenzie et al. model --  "An integrated model of habitat and species occurrence dynamics" -- would be an obvious choice, but I'd rather use R/unmarked than learn a new program :) and also, I will need to do this on many species.. so again, R is preferable. 

It is possible to use colext/dial madsen model for this type of analysis, by coding habitat based on change from t to t+1, rather than the type at t and the type at t+1? 

Has anyone done something like this? feel free to point me towards some literature... I'm just coming up blank on searches. I figure my other option is just to wait for AHM volume 2 to hit the press...  

Thanks!

Sarah Thompson

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] using colext to look at how habitat change influences occupancy dynamics
parts:
Dear Sarah,

I think that modeling colonisation/extinction by a site covariate which is the change in the habitat in the 25 year interval would be pretty straightforward and easy to do. You could put colext into a loop over species or else use BUGS and run a multi-species, or community, dynamic occupancy model (a la Dorazio et al., Ecology, 2010). I could send you code off-list: I am drafting the chapter on that model for AHM2 RIGHT NOW :)

Best regards  ---- Marc
